podcast.body: The title track of his sixth studio album, released in the fall of 1972, this song was a slow grower, taking over twelve weeks to reach the Hot 100's Top 10 by early spring 1973. More than "Take Me Home, Country Roads," this song, with its soaring melody and celebration of nature, solidified John Denver's public persona. However, the lyric "and everybody's high" caused controversy, leading to a temporary ban by the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) for perceived drug abuse promotion, despite Denver intending it to mean "high on life." This censorship limited its appeal to conservative country listeners. "Released in the fall of 1972, Rocky Mountain high was the title track to John Denver's sixth studio album and his first to crack the top 10 on the LP's chart."
